summary: Okta adaptive auth rejects developer staging logins due to device clock/timezone mismatch
summary_detail: Multiple developers report being denied access to the staging developer portal (support-console) during Okta SSO flow. Failures coincide with device timezone or clock skew on users' machines; Okta adaptive rules mark the device as anomalous and reject assertions. Affects developer productivity for staging-only workflows.
impact: ~25 developers intermittently unable to complete SSO to staging for ~8 hours during 2026-03-12 morning. Blocks deploy verification and feature QA. No production impact reported.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a laptop with the local clock deliberately set 5+ minutes ahead or behind real time (e.g., UTC offset mismatch or wrong system time).
2) Navigate to internal staging dev portal (https://dev-staging.redwood.internal) and click 'Sign in with Okta'.
3) Complete Okta multi-factor prompt when presented.
4) Observe failed redirect back to the portal with error 'Authentication rejected by policy' or see 403/unauthorized in the portal UI.
observed_behavior: Okta SSO completes MFA but the Okta adaptive access policy flags the session as 'device time inconsistent' and denies token issuance. End-user sees a generic 'Access denied by your organization' page and support logs show 401/403 on the redirect endpoint. Some clients report 'invalid_grant' when the portal exchanges the code for tokens.
expected_behavior: Users with valid Okta credentials and MFA should successfully authenticate to the staging dev portal regardless of minor local clock skew (within reasonable bounds), or we should present a clearer remediation path rather than a silent deny.

investigation_notes: - Triage lead reproduced locally by setting macOS system clock 7 minutes in future => identical failure path observed.

- Okta policy 'adaptive_device_time_mismatch' appears to be a custom adaptive rule triggered by device time drift above threshold; policy was recently adjusted in policy-change roll on 2026-03-10 (see INT-1129000 audit).
- Affected users primarily use older developer laptops (Windows 10, macOS 11) that sometimes lose NTP sync after sleeping/waking or VPN transitions to staging network.
- No anomalies found in the staging identity provider connector logs besides policy denials; token service itself healthy in metrics.
reproduction_attempts: Attempt 1 (Aisha): reproduced with local clock +7min => policy DENY and 403 returned to portal.
Attempt 2 (SRE): reproduced with containerized Chromium with TZ set incorrectly => same policy hit.
Attempt 3 (Support): corrected client clock (ntpdate) and user could successfully sign in.
root_cause_hypothesis: Okta adaptive access rule enforces strict device time consistency. Recent policy tightening (post INT-1129000 change) lowered tolerated clock skew. Many staging dev machines are vulnerable to transient NTP drift, causing otherwise-valid sessions to be denied.
workaround: Users can immediately fix by syncing system clock (macOS: 'sudo sntp -sS time.apple.com' or 'System Preferences → Date & Time → Set date and time automatically'; Windows: toggle 'Set time automatically' or run 'w32tm /resync'). Support can temporarily add users to an Okta bypass group (see runbook) if they cannot update their device.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Support runbook: guidance steps to resync clocks and temporary Okta bypass group flow documented at https://confluence.redwood.internal/okta/device-time-runbook
2) Create automation ticket to add an 'Okta-bypass-staging' group for verified developers so Support can add members quickly (manual approval required).
3) Inform devs via #support and #devs-staging Slack channels with clear instructions.
long_term_action_items: - Product Security / Identity to review adaptive rule thresholds and determine safe skew tolerance for non-production environments.
- Engineering to add client-side check in dev-portal that detects large local clock skew and surfaces a targeted remediation UI before redirecting to Okta.
- SRE to schedule NTP/chrony sanity check into the developer laptop onboarding doc and agent images.
